title: Screen Printing — One Spark

scenes.title: Print run: one spark becomes a connected system
scenes.purpose: Show a three-screen print run on cool blue-gray recycled stock: teal and vermilion-orange spot inks overprint, then a paper-tone ink draws a light bulb that turns into a network.
visuals: Cool blue-gray recycled paper with a fixed fibre texture
Teal ink screen: right-hand field and the word ONE
Vermilion-orange ink screen in multiply: big disc (it overprints the teal into a near-black mixed tone), a diagonal hatch band with a knocked-out label box, and the word SPARK
Opaque paper-tone ink: bulb, network links and nodes
Orange detail pull: filament and node centres

beats.development: The teal squeegee pull wipes left to right. It lays down the word ONE, then the rough-edged teal field.

The orange screen pulls top to bottom and slides into registration. The disc overprints the teal into a dark mixed tone, SPARK prints, and the hatch band leaves a paper knockout box. Once the box is complete, the label wipes in inside it.
The paper-tone bulb settles. Network links draw out from it, and each node disc pops in when its link reaches it. Last, the orange filament and node centres overprint.
The finished print holds still so the full title and the system can be read.
captions: ONE SPARK BECOMES A CONNECTED SYSTEM

findings: Each ink pass is one readable action, and passes overlap slightly, the way press pulls follow each other.
All copy is fully printed by 1.34 s and stays still afterwards.
Network growth is staggered by link arrival, so the eye follows the path from bulb to system.
justifiedHolds: 2.3–3.0 s: final reading hold on the completed print.

notes: Grain, paper fibre and ink-edge roughness are fixed. Seeded textures are never re-randomized.
